nodes.text: voices in a crowded room
"Give me a reason. Give me one fucking reason. Ain't got one?

"That's okay. People like you got em even if you can't say the goddamn words. I've served on juries, I've gone to third world countries, I've even set foot in a ghetto slum, so I know what poor people look like, what they sound like, and what they don't do for a living.
"You Miss, are a good for nothing bum. You don't shop so much as you scavenge. It's all about the handout, isn't it?

"It's all about popping out bastard kids and wearing stretch pants and being a hundred and fifty pounds overweight, even though you have no money to buy food, so you expect the government to give you food, because getting something for nothing is what you live for.
"You want to amount to nothing, good, because you might as well kill yourself now. It's a goddamn shame people like you have to exist for the rest of us to matter. Goddamn."

"It's hard to understand things that are not connected to us, have never been a part of our lives. We've actually got to learn how to connect to people, places, ideas. Hate is sort of the disconnect that happens.
"Not when we make the effort not to learn, but when we choose to remove those people, places and ideas from ourselves entirely. It hurts to breathe sometimes, thinking about how much people hate us.

"How what we do and say won't make a whit of a difference, how even if they have us at their mercy, they'll go ahead and kill our children in front of us just for spite. It doesn't matter how we talk, how we look, what we believe, because we're all the same really.

"Because someone out there hates you no matter who you are. Because all you can do is try and stay alive, try and not cross paths with the person or persons who will undo you. Because this isn't about paranoia, it's about survival.
"It's about history and who we are. There's a reason we believe in the end of the world. It's about being a faceless individual in a heartless society.

"It's about being a person in your own mind, waging war against yourself, where yourself is never constant, where what you believe is just energy tap dancing across tiny tendrils of flesh. What you perceive isn't real, it's just a delusion of what you want to be real.
"It's reality motivated by your own petty desires and dreams. It isn't what the rest of us want. We want to be better than you.
"And in the end, we will crush you and you will be dead. Another tragedy, another disconnection from the life we lead."
"Babies laugh and cry, but they can't sing. I've never heard a baby sing. I wonder if babies even know what music is.

"It's just noise to the baby and maybe all of life is just noise to the baby. They say a baby's brain is formed in the last three months of pregnancy, before that it really doesn't have a human brain, not really. When a baby is not a baby, it can start to sing and dance and play.

"Before that it's just cute and tender and stupid. They say playing music for a baby will make that baby grow up smarter, like maybe noise is what makes us smarter. There are plenty of smart deaf people, but before, back in the day, they called them deaf and dumb, like maybe the two were connected somehow.

"Maybe that's just how they were perceived. Because nobody did nothing for them. Maybe filling up some baby's head with noise, keeping them surrounded by words and sounds and compositions of music, maybe that can have some effect on how they come to be.
"Maybe the same can be true for the opposite, being alone with yourself, the senses you rely on for company. Babies have the possibility of the world in them. Everything and nothing."
The room is loud and nobody is looking at anybody.
"Saw a man once, man with a stick for a hand. Not like a hook or nothing. A stick, like a twig, only bigger than a twig.
"It just came out of his wrist. I'm sure it was hygienic and had some sort of purpose, but it didn't look it. Looked like he had a goddamn stick for a hand.

"Didn't look like he belonged in this world. Looked like something out of a horror movie, or some cave drawing. Having a stick for a hand has to be symbolic of something, but didn't seem that way to me.
"It didn't even look like a sturdy stick. Like maybe it might break at any second. He couldn't use it for nothing, except scaring kids with.

"I kept thinking if he fell down, he'd probably try and stop his fall with his stick hand, and break that stick, or worse, drive that stick even deeper into the stump. Maybe he was some sort of circus freak show person, maybe some masochist who does that to himself for the attention. Probably not.
"Probably just some guy. Only difference being his stick for a hand."
"I'm looking for something. Anything. Because nothing fills the void.
"I'm programmed to want. I'm programmed to desire more than I can have. And having nothing hurts me.
"It gnaws at me. I'm not going hungry. I'm not ignorant.
"I just want what I can't have. I am nothing because I have nothing. I haven't had sex in over three years.
"I don't drive a nice car. I live in a run down apartment and eat grilled cheese and macaroni and cheese. I steal ketchup packets from fast food places.
"I steal straws for God's sake. It doesn't make any sense. Because I'm not really poor, in the grand scheme of things.

"I wasn't born in Somalia for God's sake. I'm not living in my Mother's basement any more, but I might as well be. I have credit card debt, and school debt and I think I owe the IRS still, for some strange stock thing I can't explain.

"Because I wasn't even making enough to file at the time, and yet they still want money from me. I have nightmares about repossession and my teeth falling out. I dream about days off where I can sit at home and do nothing but watch television and jerk off.
"Because I don't want to kill myself, but I don't want to be alive any longer. I'm twenty four and I look at my father and I think he's had a much better life than me. Maybe that's what I need to do.

"Become a father, become a caregiver to a child who doesn't want to be here. Because I think maybe some people are happier never being born. Like maybe things just get worse the moment you're conceived.
"Because it can only end one way."
"Nothing is happening. You repeat to yourself, nothing is happening. This is going nowhere.
"These people mean nothing. Their lives, their words, they count for shit. And you'd be right.
"Damn right. They depress me. They bring me down and take me away from where I want to be.
"But the petty and insignificant are our friends and family. They are the people who aren't us. They are people we write letters to once a year and push to the backs of our memory.

"We can never be less than perfect, never immaculate for more than an hour out of the day. Depression is a sickness and it can be treated with self help. We just have to read books about how to get better, attend seminars with survivors who have stories to share.
"Don't fall into the abyss. Don't lose yourself in your sorrow. To stop caring is to stop living.
"Pay attention to the voices around you. Listen to what they have to say, even if it doesn't make any sense. Because to them, it does.
"Because to them, they've got to share. This is about healing. This is about returning to yourself."
